title: Why does the Moon change shape?
one_idea: The Moon doesn't change shape — we see different amounts of its sunlit side as it orbits Earth.
audience_misconception: Kids often think the Moon physically grows and shrinks, or that clouds cover parts of it.

analogy.source_term: The Moon reflects sunlight and we see different amounts of its lit side as it orbits.
mapping: A bright flashlight held by someone
A round cookie held at arm's length
A child walking around the table
The part of the cookie the flashlight lights up
analogy.limitation: A cookie is flat but the Moon is a ball — and unlike a cookie, nothing actually touches the Moon to change it.

direction.mode_reason: A child gazing up at the changing Moon creates a relatable moment of wonder; the mystery hook suits the cold-open format.

claims.claim: The Moon does not produce its own light; it reflects sunlight.
As the Moon orbits Earth, we see different portions of its sunlit side, creating the phases.
A full moon occurs when we see the entire sunlit side of the Moon from Earth.

mechanism.step: The Moon reflects sunlight rather than making its own light.
As the Moon travels around Earth, our view of the sunlit part changes.
Different amounts of the lit side face Earth, so the Moon looks like it changes shape.

concepts.name: moon phases
concepts.definition: The different shapes we see when we look at the Moon, from a tiny sliver to a full circle.

concepts.name: sunlight reflection
concepts.definition: When the Moon bounces light from the Sun back toward Earth.
